findings.title: enableSqlExpressions is dead logic and always returns false
findings.body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` in both branches, making the feature-toggle check meaningless dead code. Since the intent of the PR is to disable SQL expressions entirely, this is misleading: readers and linters will assume the flag still has an effect. Either remove the function and the toggle check entirely (and return an unconditional error), or actually honor the flag if that was intended. As written it also guarantees the QueryTypeSQL path can never be enabled, which should be stated clearly in the code rather than hidden behind dead branches.

findings.title: Feature-disable check not applied to UnmarshalSQLCommand / legacy path
findings.body: The new disable check was only added to `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` (pkg/expr/reader.go, QueryTypeSQL case). However `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (pkg/expr/sql_command.go) also constructs `SQLCommand` from user-supplied query JSON (`rn.Query["expression"]`) and does not perform any feature-toggle or disable check. If any code path (e.g. older frontend payloads handled through the raw-node unmarshal route in transform.go/parse.go) still dispatches to `UnmarshalSQLCommand` for `type: "sql"`, a user can still create SQL commands; while the stub DB now fails at Execute time, the parsing/validation code is still reachable and the intended hard disable is inconsistent. The disable should be enforced at command-construction level (or both entry points), not only one reader.

findings.title: Error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is wrong/misleading
findings.body: When a user submits a SQL expression, they get `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"`. The feature is implemented but disabled for security reasons (CVE-2024-9264). The message should say something like "SQL expressions are disabled" so users understand this is a deliberate state and can find the associated documentation/flag. The current wording will generate confusion and unnecessary support issues.

findings.title: Execute overwrites NoData result with empty TableData
findings.body: In `SQLCommand.Execute`, when `frame.Rows() == 0` the code sets `rsp.Values` to a `NoData` value, but then unconditionally overwrites `rsp.Values` with `TableData{Frame: frame}` on the next statement (lines 116-118). The NoData branch is dead code and downstream consumers will see an empty table instead of a NoData result. This is pre-existing, but since this PR touches Execute and leaves it in place, it is worth fixing while here.

findings.title: No tests updated for disabled SQL expressions; existing tests will fail or are now meaningless
findings.body: The PR replaces the DuckDB-backed implementation with stubs that always return "not implemented", and removes the go-duck dependency, but includes no test changes. Any existing tests in pkg/expr/sql (TablesList) or SQL-command integration/e2e tests will now fail because RunCommands/QueryFramesInto always error. Additionally there are no new tests asserting that a QueryTypeSQL expression is rejected with the expected error from ReadQuery, nor that the legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path is blocked. A security-disable change should come with regression tests proving the CVE vector is closed.

findings.title: SQL injection-prone string interpolation left in TablesList
findings.body: `TablesList` still builds a DuckDB command via `fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)` after only escaping single quotes. Although the stub DB now makes this unreachable-at-runtime, the unsafe interpolation pattern remains in the codebase and will be silently revived when a real implementation replaces the stub. The method should either be removed along with the DuckDB dependency, or rewritten to use parameterized command execution. Also note `ast[0]` in tablesFromAST panics on an empty AST slice.
